summary: ODF-owned three-story enclosed cab on Henkle Butte, Deschutes County, OR, built 1961 to replace a 40-foot live-in tower; 1958 lightning fire spotted; not open to the public.

access.note: Not accessible to the public per an October 2021 visit report. Viewable from the road. Much of the area is private property; posted signs should be respected. Summit access is unclear.

visit.trail_note: No public approach is documented. View from the road only and respect posted signs on private property.

events.note: First live-in tower, 42 ft with an L-4 cab, built from recycled material by the CCC (Roaming Civic). firelookout.com and the Bulletin say the 1940s, 40 ft; NHLR gives no date
Newspaper item quoted on the Oregon Lookouts page: 1953 season opened; a lookout signed on for her third year
July 8, 1958 lightning fire broke out again about two miles northeast of Three Creeks Butte, on Brooks-Scanlon land; the Henkle Butte lookout discovered it
Current three-story enclosed ODF cab built in 1961, replacing the 40-foot live-in tower
Registered September 4, 2011 as NHLR US 915, OR 119
Bulletin profile: a lookout manning the cab mid-June through October, seven days a week
Visit October 9, 2021: currently standing; not accessible to the public; viewable from the road

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com says five miles northeast of Sisters and a 1953 newspaper item says six miles north. A 2014 Bulletin article says roughly a mile northeast. The story gives the first two and flags the third.

The first tower is 40 feet in the register, firelookout.com and the Bulletin, and 42 feet in the Roaming Civic. The 1940s date (firelookout.com, Bulletin) differs from 1943 (Roaming Civic). The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Record height_m 12.2 is not supported by any page read here, so it is not in facts; check its source. Elevation 1040.0 m matches NHLR (3,412 ft / 1,040 m). Location conflict: NHLR says 'north of Bend'; firelookout.com and a 1953 item say 5-6 miles from Sisters; the 2014 Bulletin says roughly a mile. The first tower's height (40 vs 42 ft) and date (1940s vs 1943) conflict. A 2020 Central Oregonian search snippet says the first lookout was built in the 1930s; it was not read and is not cited. The 1953 and 1958 lookouts and the 2014 staffer are named in the sources; their names are left out. Access 'restricted' comes from one 2021 blog visit; no ODF statement was read. Name origin rests on the Roaming Civic alone.
